result:
My grandmother kept her buttons in a tobacco tin. You could tell when she was looking for one because she tipped the whole lot onto the kitchen table. It sounded like a cup of teeth.

Once, when I was nine, she asked me to find a button for the cuff of her good coat. The other cuff had a brown one, plain except for a little raised rim. I found its twin almost immediately, but I also found a blue glass button with a ship on it. The ship had three sails. I put both buttons in her palm.

“Well,” she said, “which would you rather look at on the bus?”

For years afterward she wore that ship just above her left glove. I liked sitting beside her when she raised her hand to pull the cord for our stop.

I have the coat now. The lining has given way under one arm, and there’s a boiled sweet in the pocket that has achieved the hardness and possibly the age of amber. Last winter the brown button came off in my hand. I went through the tin looking for its twin. It was still there.

So was a little green fish.
